items.outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works
items.title: What They're Saying: Bipartisan Permitting Reform Will Deliver Cheaper Energy, More Jobs, Responsible Growth
items.summary: Majority roundup of supportive quotes from business, energy, labor, housing, county, state and think-tank groups on the bill. Quotes are the groups' own statements as reproduced by the committee.

quote.text: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act delivers cheaper energy, more well-paying jobs, and responsible growth by accelerating the permitting and construction of critical energy and infrastructure projects while maintaining key environmental and historic preservation safeguards.
quote.speaker: EPW majority press office

items.outlet: Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources (Democrats)
items.title: What They're Saying: Heinrich's Bipartisan Permitting Reform Deal Will Deliver Cheaper Energy, More Jobs, Responsible Growth
items.summary: Democratic-side version of the supportive roundup, published October 9, with the same group quotes as the committee's October 7 release.

quote.text: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act delivers cheaper energy, more well-paying jobs, and responsible growth by accelerating the permitting and construction of critical energy and infrastructure projects while maintaining key environmental and historic preservation safeguards.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich's office (press release)

items.author: Brandon Tatum
items.title: NGA Statement on Permitting Reform
items.summary: NGA's CEO, Brandon Tatum, issued a statement welcoming the bill's introduction and saying NGA will work with Congress on it.

quote.text: The National Governors Association and its partners are encouraged by the introduction of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 and look forward to working with Congress to further develop this legislation.
quote.speaker: Brandon Tatum, NGA CEO

items.author: State of Montana Newsroom
items.title: Gianforte urges Congress to pass federal permitting reform
items.summary: Montana Gov. Greg Gianforte said he joined 21 other governors in a joint statement urging Congress to pass permitting reform and send the bill to the President. The release describes the signers as Republican governors.

quote.text: Republican governors are working every day to cut red tape, increase investment, and make our states the best places in the world to build, innovate, and do business.
quote.speaker: Joint statement of Republican governors (Gov. Greg Gianforte, Montana)

letter.ask: Republican governors urge Congress to act swiftly, pass meaningful permitting reform, and send this legislation to President Trump's desk.

items.author: Bill Owens
items.title: NAHB Applauds Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
items.summary: NAHB's chairman praised the four sponsors for crafting the most meaningful federal permitting reforms in decades.

quote.text: NAHB applauds Senators Lee, Capito, Heinrich and Whitehouse and for their leadership and bipartisan approach to crafting the most meaningful reforms in decades to several key federal environmental permitting programs.
quote.speaker: Bill Owens, NAHB chairman

items.title: The Crucial Hardhat Union That Has Yet to Endorse the Permitting Bill
items.summary: Heatmap reports the IBEW has not endorsed the bill. An IBEW spokesperson said the union is reviewing the language and holding discussions with stakeholders.

quote.text: reviewing the language and holding discussions with stakeholders across our industries.
quote.speaker: IBEW spokesperson (unnamed)

items.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026: Permitting Reform County Advocacy Hub
items.summary: NACo's advocacy hub, published October 8, summarizes the bill's county provisions, including a guarantee of cooperating-agency status for counties in NEPA reviews, and gives a template letter urging senators to support it.

quote.text: Contact your senators and urge them to support the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
quote.speaker: National Association of Counties (advocacy hub)

items.outlet: Common Dreams (newswire, reprinting Center for Biological Diversity release)
items.author: Center for Biological Diversity; Friends of the Earth
items.title: Hundreds of Organizations Oppose Endangered Species Attacks in Permitting Legislation
items.summary: More than 200 conservation organizations sent a letter urging Congress to oppose the bill over its Endangered Species Act provisions. The release was issued by the Center for Biological Diversity and Friends of the Earth.

quote.text: The bill includes sweeping attacks on the Endangered Species Act that would gut protections for nearly every endangered species across the country.
quote.speaker: Center for Biological Diversity and Friends of the Earth (joint release)

letter.ask: Oppose the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 over its Endangered Species Act provisions.

items.author: Native American Rights Fund
items.title: ACT NOW: Senate Permitting Reform Bill Negatively Impacts Tribes
items.summary: NARF's October 15 page reports that NARF and eight other Tribal organizations sent an October 9 letter asking Senate leaders to remove provisions that would weaken protections for sacred places, and links the joint letter.

quote.text: The BAAJA severely weakens Tribal opportunities to engage as sovereign governments, curtails Tribal consultation requirements, and restricts access to legal recourse in court.
quote.speaker: Native American Rights Fund

signers_sample: National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers
letter.ask: Remove provisions of the bill that would weaken protections for sacred places.

items.title: 185 Groups Slam Permitting Bill's Sweetheart Deal for Data Centers
items.summary: A coalition of 185 groups urged congressional leaders to oppose the bill, calling it a 'back-door deal' to drive buildout of AI data centers and fossil fuel infrastructure. The release lists the coalition's leading groups; the letter PDF was not readable.

quote.text: A coalition of 185 community, labor, climate and environmental justice organizations today urged congressional leaders to oppose anti-environmental permitting legislation.
quote.speaker: Center for Biological Diversity (press release)

letter.to: congressional leaders (release); House Democratic leadership (Washington Sun)
letter.ask: Oppose anti-environmental permitting legislation, which the release identifies as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act.

items.author: Sen. Roger Wicker
items.title: Wicker Backs Landmark Permit Reform Bill
items.summary: Sen. Wicker's weekly report backs the bill as landmark permit reform, saying it would shorten the window for climate litigation to 150 days and narrow Clean Water Act reviews.

quote.text: would fundamentally update the way the government approves new domestic energy and infrastructure projects.
quote.speaker: Sen. Roger Wicker (R-MS)

items.author: Save the Manatee Club
items.title: Opposition Statement: S. 5653, Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
items.summary: The club opposes S. 5653 and urges all members of Congress, especially the Florida Delegation, to oppose it.

quote.text: We respectfully urge all members of Congress, especially the Florida Delegation, to oppose this dangerous legislation.
quote.speaker: Save the Manatee Club

items.author: NPR
items.title: U.S. historic preservation law faces the most serious threat in its 60-year history
items.summary: NPR reports the bill's Section 106 provisions as the biggest threat to historic preservation review in 60 years, quotes NATHPO's executive director, and reports that a letter from NATHPO and other tribal groups went to Senate leaders the prior week.

quote.text: It will effectively rewrite the National Historic Preservation Act in ways that, for all intents and purposes, gut its meaning and protections for hundreds of thousands of sites across the country,
quote.speaker: Greg Werkheiser, Cultural Heritage Partners

items.author: The Washington Sun
items.title: Permitting Reform Is Scrambling the Left
items.summary: The Washington Sun reports that major green groups have hedged on the bill, and that the Sierra Club's stance is a marked departure from its earlier criticism. It reports a letter from 185 organizations to House Democratic leadership.

quote.text: Major green groups — the League of Conservation Voters, the Sierra Club, the Environmental Defense Fund, the Natural Resources Defense Council — have hedged.
quote.speaker: The Washington Sun (reporting)

items.title: On Historic Preservation Law's 60th Anniversary, 1,000 Organizations Launch Campaign to Defend America's Heritage
items.summary: The 106 Strong coalition launched on the NHPA's 60th anniversary with 1,000 participating organizations and Tribal Nations, and delivered a letter to Congress calling for the defeat of S. 5653. The coalition's count is its own.

quote.text: Section 106 asks our government to do something profoundly reasonable: stop, look, and listen before destroying places Americans value,
quote.speaker: Greg Werkheiser

signers_sample: National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers
letter.ask: Defeat S. 5653, which the letter says would remove the public's voice from Section 106 review and attack Tribal sovereignty.

items.title: Support for the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
items.summary: The Chamber's support page backs the bill and urges Congress to pass it.

quote.text: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to fix our broken permitting system.
quote.speaker: U.S. Chamber of Commerce (support page)

items.author: American Supply Association
items.title: ASA Supports Bipartisan Permitting Reform to Strengthen U.S. Manufacturing
items.summary: The American Supply Association says it joined a coalition including the National Association of Manufacturers in a letter to Senate Majority Leader Thune and Minority Leader Schumer urging them to bring the bill to the floor without delay.

quote.text: Our members need reliable energy and water infrastructure, along with policies that spur investment.
quote.speaker: Steve Rossi, ASA VP of Advocacy

letter.to: Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer
letter.ask: Bring the measure to the Senate floor without delay.

items.title: Statement from Climate and Energy SVP Josh Freed on Environmental Group Opposition to Bipartisan Permitting Deal
items.summary: Third Way's climate and energy SVP responds to environmental-group opposition, arguing the bill would mainly benefit transmission and clean energy expansion.

quote.text: This opposition ignores the fact that the bill will be overwhelmingly beneficial to transmission and clean energy expansion in the United States.
quote.speaker: Third Way (press statement, Josh Freed)

events.title: 22 Republican governors issue joint statement urging Congress to pass permitting bill
events.summary: Montana Gov. Greg Gianforte and 21 other Republican governors issued a joint statement urging Congress to pass the bill and send it to President Trump's desk. The release says the 21 others join Gianforte, for 22 signers in total.
events.significance: A bloc of governors endorsing the bill signals state-level support from one party only.

sources.title: Gianforte urges Congress to pass federal permitting reform

events.title: More than 200 conservation groups letter urges Congress to oppose bill over ESA
events.summary: More than 200 conservation organizations sent a letter urging Congress to oppose the bill, citing its Endangered Species Act title, including a weakened 'best available science' mandate and state-run Section 7 consultations. The Center for Biological Diversity and Friends of the Earth issued the release.
events.significance: A separate conservation letter from the 185-group letter of October 13 and the 200+ letter of October 5, which is held.

sources.title: Hundreds of Organizations Oppose Endangered Species Attacks in Permitting Legislation

events.title: NARF and eight tribal organizations urge Senate leaders to strip sacred-places provisions
events.summary: In an October 9 letter, NARF and eight other Tribal organizations asked Senate leaders to remove provisions of the bill that would weaken protections for sacred places. NPR reported that NATHPO and other tribal groups sent a letter to Senate leaders the prior week.
events.significance: Targets the bill's National Historic Preservation Act title, including Section 106 consultation changes.
actors: National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers

sources.title: ACT NOW: Senate Permitting Reform Bill Negatively Impacts Tribes
U.S. historic preservation law faces the most serious threat in its 60-year history

events.title: 185 groups send congressional leaders letter opposing permitting bill as a back-door deal
events.summary: A coalition of 185 community, labor, climate and environmental justice organizations urged congressional leaders to oppose the bill, calling it a back-door deal to drive a buildout of hyperscale AI data centers and fossil fuel infrastructure.
events.significance: Addressee differs by source: the release says congressional leaders, and the Washington Sun says House Democratic leadership. The letter PDF was not readable, so the addressee and signer list are unverified beyond the release.

sources.title: 185 Groups Slam Permitting Bill's Sweetheart Deal for Data Centers
Permitting Reform Is Scrambling the Left

events.title: 106 Strong coalition launches with 1,000 organizations and urges Congress to defeat S. 5653
events.summary: On the NHPA's 60th anniversary, the 106 Strong coalition launched with 1,000 organizations and Tribal Nations, and delivered a letter to Congress calling for the defeat of S. 5653.
events.significance: The coalition's Section 106 campaign began in August with a letter of 600+ organizations (not in this window); the October figure is the coalition's own count.

sources.title: On Historic Preservation Law's 60th Anniversary, 1,000 Organizations Launch Campaign to Defend America's Heritage
U.S. historic preservation law faces the most serious threat in its 60-year history

events.title: American Supply Association joins coalition letter urging Thune and Schumer to bring bill to floor
events.summary: The American Supply Association said it joined a coalition, including the National Association of Manufacturers, in a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Minority Leader Chuck Schumer urging them to bring the bill to the floor without delay.
events.significance: Adds a trade-association signatory to the NAM-led business push; the letter's own signer count is not stated on the ASA page.

sources.title: ASA Supports Bipartisan Permitting Reform to Strengthen U.S. Manufacturing

events.title: NACo publishes county advocacy hub urging counties to contact senators on the bill
events.summary: The National Association of Counties published a permitting reform advocacy hub for the bill, urging county leaders to contact their senators, and noting the bill would guarantee counties cooperating-agency status in NEPA reviews.
events.significance: Counties are one of the few local-government groups with a published position in this window.

sources.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026: Permitting Reform County Advocacy Hub

events.title: IBEW says it is still reviewing bill language and has not endorsed
events.summary: An IBEW spokesperson told Heatmap the union is reviewing the language and holding discussions with stakeholders across its industries. Heatmap reports the union has not endorsed the bill.
events.significance: Utility and transmission labor is the open labor question in the House, per Heatmap.

sources.title: The Crucial Hardhat Union That Has Yet to Endorse the Permitting Bill
